fr.B: Il y avait au pays d’Outs un homme nommé Job. Il était intègre et droit ; il craignait Dieu et se détournait du mal.

vi.R: Ngày xưa, ở xứ Út-xơ có một người tên là Gióp. Ông trọn vẹn và ngay thẳng. Ông tôn kính Đức Chúa Trời và tránh xa điều ác.

ko.L: 우스 땅에 한 사람이 있었는데, 그의 이름은 욥이었다. 그 사람은 흠 없고 정직하여, 하나님을 경외하고 악에서 떠난 사람이었다.
ko.B: 우스 땅에 욥이라는 사람이 있었다. 그는 흠 없고 정직했으며, 하나님을 경외하고 악에서 떠났다.
ko.R: 옛날 우스 땅에 욥이라는 사람이 살았다. 그는 흠 없고 정직한 사람이었다. 그는 하나님을 두려운 마음으로 섬기고 악한 일을 멀리했다.

pt.L: Havia um homem na terra de Uz cujo nome era Jó; e aquele homem era íntegro e reto, e temia a Deus e se desviava do mal.
pt.B: Na terra de Uz havia um homem chamado Jó. Ele era íntegro e reto; temia a Deus e se desviava do mal.
pt.R: Na terra de Uz vivia um homem chamado Jó. Ele era íntegro e reto. Honrava a Deus e se mantinha longe do mal.

decisions.choice: the land of Uz: a land east of Israel; Job is not an Israelite
decisions.reason: Uz is a name linked both with Aram (Genesis 10:23; 22:21) and with Edom (Genesis 36:28; Lamentations 4:21, "daughter of Edom, who lives in the land of Uz"), so it lay somewhere to the east or southeast of Israel; its exact place is not known. The story is set outside Israel, gives no date, and never mentions Israel's history, law or temple. Job and his friends are wise men of the East (1:3; 2:11).

decisions.choice: blameless and upright: whole in character and straight in conduct, not sinless
decisions.reason: The first word describes what is whole and complete, with nothing lacking; of a person it means integrity, a life that is all of one piece (Genesis 25:27; Psalm 37:37). Its noun is the "integrity" Job holds fast to (2:3, 9; 27:5; 31:6), and the question of the whole book is whether that integrity is real. The second word means straight, honest, doing what is right. Neither word claims that Job never sinned: he offers sacrifices in case of sin (1:5) and later speaks of the sins of his youth (13:26). God repeats the same description (1:8; 2:3).

decisions.choice: feared God and turned away from evil: reverent obedience to God
decisions.reason: To fear God is to hold him in awe and so to obey him; it is the beginning of wisdom (Proverbs 1:7; 9:10), and Job 28:28 joins the same two phrases: "the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding". The participles describe Job's settled way of life, not a single act.

decisions.choice: blameless and upright at every level
alternatives: honest and did what was right (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Blameless" is the book's theme word; keeping it at every level lets Readable readers hear it again at 1:8, 2:3 and in Job's speeches. Readable keeps "upright" beside it, as the fixed pair of the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: honored God; kept away from evil (Readable)
decisions.reason: For a new reader "feared God" can sound like terror. Readable says "honored God", the respect and obedience the phrase means; Literal and Balanced keep "feared God".

decisions.choice: "íntegro y recto" at every level; "temía a Dios y se apartaba del mal" (L, B), "honraba a Dios y se alejaba del mal" (R)
decisions.reason: The book's theme words keep one Spanish wording through Job so readers hear them again at 1:8, 2:3 and in the speeches; "íntegro" says whole in character, not sinless, which "perfecto" would suggest. Readable says "honraba" as the English says "honored", following Proverbs 3:7.

decisions.choice: "tú" to each single person (God, Job, each friend); a plural_you span wherever several are addressed
decisions.reason: Job's speakers address one another and God with "tú" throughout the book. Where a speech addresses a group (Job to his three friends, Elihu to the three, God to the friends in 42:7-8), the verbs, pronouns and possessives take a plural_you span, "ustedes" by default with "vosotros" as the alternative.

decisions.choice: Narrative tenses: passé simple at Literal and Balanced, passé composé at Readable; imparfait for states and repeated action (1:4-5)
decisions.reason: Job 1-2 and 42:7-17 are narrative. Literal and Balanced use the literary narrative tense, Readable the spoken past tense of everyday French; the speeches from chapter 3 on use present, future and passé composé at every level.

decisions.choice: "intègre et droit" at every level; "craignait Dieu et se détournait du mal" (L, B), "honorait Dieu et se tenait loin du mal" (R)
decisions.reason: One wording for the book's theme pair, kept at every level so the word returns at 1:8, 2:3 and 27:5; "intègre" says integrity, not sinlessness. Readable says "honorait" for the fear of God, as Proverbs 3:7 does.

decisions.choice: "mkamilifu na mnyofu" at every level; "alimcha Mungu na kujiepusha na uovu" (L, B), "alimheshimu Mungu na kukaa mbali na uovu" (R)
decisions.reason: One wording for the book's theme pair through Job. "Kumcha Mungu" is the settled phrase for the fear of God; Readable says "kumheshimu", as in Proverbs 3:7.

decisions.choice: "trọn vẹn và ngay thẳng" at every level; "kính sợ Đức Chúa Trời và lánh xa điều ác" (L, B), "tôn kính Đức Chúa Trời và tránh xa điều ác" (R)
decisions.reason: One wording for the book's theme pair through Job; "trọn vẹn" is wholeness of character, not sinlessness. Readable says "tôn kính" for the fear of God, as Proverbs 3:7 does.

decisions.choice: Job is "ông" in the narrative (Balanced, Readable); Literal keeps "người ấy" for "that man"
decisions.reason: A respected older man is referred to as "ông" in Vietnamese narrative; Literal follows the Hebrew's "the man".

decisions.choice: "흠 없고 정직하다" at every level; "하나님을 경외하고 악에서 떠났다" (L, B), "하나님을 두려운 마음으로 섬기고 악한 일을 멀리했다" (R)
decisions.reason: One wording for the book's theme pair through Job; "흠 없다" says blameless in character, not sinless. Readable unpacks "경외" for new readers, as in Proverbs 3:7.

decisions.choice: Narrative in the plain written style (-었다), with -시- and 께서 for God; speech levels by relationship (God 해라체, people to God 합쇼체, Job and his friends 하오체)
decisions.reason: The book's settled speech levels: the narrator is neutral and plain, honouring only God; each scene keeps the same relationship from verse to verse.

decisions.choice: "íntegro e reto" at every level; "temia a Deus e se desviava do mal" (L, B), "honrava a Deus e se mantinha longe do mal" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: one wording for the theme pair, repeated unchanged at 1:8 and 2:3 and wherever Job's integrity returns, so readers hear the same words. "Íntegro" is whole in character, the sense of m2 (and the word used of Abraham at Genesis 17:1); "perfeito" would suggest sinlessness. "Se desviava do mal" keeps the picture of turning aside. Readable says "honrava a Deus" as the English Readable says "honored", since "temer" can sound like terror.

decisions.choice: Uz; Jó
decisions.reason: The Brazilian forms of the names: "Uz" as in Genesis 10:23 and 36:28, "Jó" as Portuguese has always called him. Other names in Job follow the forms of the books before it: os sabeus, os caldeus, Temã (Genesis 36:11).

pt.B: Ele teve sete filhos e três filhas.
pt.R: Ele teve sete filhos e três filhas.

decisions.choice: seven sons and three daughters: a complete and blessed family
decisions.reason: Many sons were counted a sign of God's blessing (Psalm 127:3-5; Ruth 4:15; 1 Samuel 2:5). Seven and three, which add up to ten, are numbers of fullness, and the same numbers of children are given to Job again at the end (42:13). The numbers of his flocks in the next verse follow the same pattern.

decisions.choice: He had (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "there were born to him", which Literal keeps; Balanced and Readable use the plain English way of saying it.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י מִ֠קְנֵהוּ שִֽׁבְעַ֨ת אַלְפֵי־צֹ֜אן וּשְׁלֹ֧שֶׁת אַלְפֵ֣י גְמַלִּ֗ים וַחֲמֵ֨שׁ מֵא֤וֹת צֶֽמֶד־בָּקָר֙ וַחֲמֵ֣שׁ מֵא֣וֹת אֲתוֹנ֔וֹת וַעֲבֻדָּ֖ה רַבָּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד וַיְהִי֙ הָאִ֣ישׁ הַה֔וּא גָּד֖וֹל מִכָּל־בְּנֵי־קֶֽדֶם׃

records.literal_gloss: And was his livestock seven thousand(s) [of] sheep and three thousand(s) [of] camels and five hundred yoke[s] of oxen and five hundred female donkeys, and service [was] very much; and was the man that great more than all [the] sons of [the] east.

en.L: And his livestock was 7,000 sheep and 3,000 camels and 500 yoke of oxen and 500 female donkeys, and very many servants; and that man was greater than all the sons of the east.
en.B: He owned 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 yoke of oxen and 500 female donkeys, and he had a great many servants. He was the greatest man among all the peoples of the East.
en.R: He owned 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 pairs of oxen and 500 female donkeys. He also had a great many servants. He was the richest and most important man in all the lands to the east.

es.R: Tenía 7 000 ovejas, 3 000 camellos, 500 pares de bueyes y 500 burras. También tenía muchísimos sirvientes. Era el hombre más rico e importante de todas las tierras del oriente.

fr.L: Et son bétail était de 7 000 moutons, 3 000 chameaux, 500 attelages de bœufs et 500 ânesses, avec des serviteurs en très grand nombre ; et cet homme était plus grand que tous les fils de l’Orient.
fr.B: Il possédait 7 000 moutons, 3 000 chameaux, 500 paires de bœufs et 500 ânesses, et il avait un très grand nombre de serviteurs. C’était l’homme le plus important de tous les peuples de l’Orient.
fr.R: Il avait 7 000 moutons, 3 000 chameaux, 500 paires de bœufs et 500 ânesses. Il avait aussi beaucoup de serviteurs. C’était l’homme le plus riche et le plus important de toutes les régions de l’Est.

sw.L: Na mifugo yake ilikuwa kondoo 7,000, ngamia 3,000, jozi 500 za ng'ombe na punda wa kike 500, na watumishi wengi sana; na mtu huyo alikuwa mkuu kuliko wana wote wa mashariki.
sw.B: Alikuwa na kondoo 7,000, ngamia 3,000, jozi 500 za ng'ombe na punda wa kike 500, tena alikuwa na watumishi wengi mno. Alikuwa mtu mkuu kuliko watu wote wa Mashariki.
sw.R: Alikuwa na kondoo 7,000, ngamia 3,000, jozi 500 za ng'ombe na punda wa kike 500. Pia alikuwa na watumishi wengi sana. Alikuwa tajiri na mashuhuri kuliko watu wote katika nchi za mashariki.

vi.L: Và gia súc của ông là 7.000 chiên, 3.000 lạc đà, 500 cặp bò và 500 lừa cái, cùng rất nhiều đầy tớ; và người ấy lớn hơn hết thảy con cái phương đông.
vi.B: Ông có 7.000 chiên, 3.000 lạc đà, 500 cặp bò và 500 lừa cái, lại có rất đông đầy tớ. Ông là người lớn nhất trong tất cả các dân phương Đông.
vi.R: Ông có 7.000 con chiên, 3.000 con lạc đà, 500 cặp bò và 500 con lừa cái. Ông cũng có rất nhiều đầy tớ. Ông là người giàu có và quyền thế nhất ở khắp các xứ phương đông.

ko.L: 그의 가축은 양 7,000마리와 낙타 3,000마리와 소 500겨리와 암나귀 500마리였고, 종도 매우 많았다. 그리고 그 사람은 동방의 모든 자손보다 더 컸다.
ko.B: 그는 양 7,000마리, 낙타 3,000마리, 소 500겨리, 암나귀 500마리를 가졌고, 종들도 매우 많았다. 그는 동방의 모든 백성 가운데 가장 큰 사람이었다.
ko.R: 그는 양 7,000마리, 낙타 3,000마리, 소 500쌍, 암나귀 500마리를 가지고 있었다. 종들도 아주 많았다. 그는 동쪽 지방 전체에서 가장 부유하고 이름난 사람이었다.

pt.L: E o seu gado era de sete mil ovelhas e três mil camelos e quinhentas juntas de bois e quinhentas jumentas, e muitíssimos servos; e aquele homem era maior que todos os filhos do oriente.
pt.B: Ele possuía sete mil ovelhas, três mil camelos, quinhentas juntas de bois e quinhentas jumentas, e tinha um grande número de servos. Era o maior homem entre todos os povos do Oriente.
pt.R: Ele tinha sete mil ovelhas, três mil camelos, quinhentos pares de bois e quinhentas jumentas. Também tinha muitos e muitos servos. Era o homem mais rico e mais importante de todas as terras do Oriente.

decisions.choice: a rich herdsman's wealth: flocks, camels, plow oxen and donkeys
decisions.reason: Wealth in the ancient East was counted in animals. The word for "sheep" covers the flock, sheep and goats together. Oxen were counted by the yoke, the pair that plows together (1:14), and female donkeys were prized for breeding and milk. Seven and three thousand repeat the numbers of his children (1:2); the totals are doubled at the end (42:12).

decisions.choice: very many servants
decisions.reason: The word means service or work, and here, as in Genesis 26:14, it stands for the people who do the work: a large household of servants. It completes the picture of a great estate.

decisions.choice: the sons of the east: the peoples living east of Israel, toward the desert
decisions.reason: The phrase names the peoples of the lands east of the Jordan and the Syrian-Arabian desert (Genesis 29:1; Judges 6:3). They were known for their wisdom (1 Kings 5:10, numbered 4:30 in many Bibles). "Great" includes wealth and standing together.

decisions.choice: pairs of oxen; the richest and most important (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Yoke" as a count is unfamiliar to many readers, so Readable says "pairs". It spells out "great" as both wealth and standing, which the verse's list of possessions shows.
"겨리" is a pair of oxen yoked to one plow, the unit the Hebrew counts by; Readable says "쌍" (pairs), the everyday word, as the English says "pairs".

source.text: וְהָלְכ֤וּ בָנָיו֙ וְעָשׂ֣וּ מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה בֵּ֖ית אִ֣ישׁ יוֹמ֑וֹ וְשָׁלְח֗וּ וְקָרְאוּ֙ לִשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת אַחְיֽוֹתֵיהֶ֔ם לֶאֱכֹ֥ל וְלִשְׁתּ֖וֹת עִמָּהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And went his sons and made a feast [at the] house of each one [on] his day, and they sent and called to [the] three of their sisters to eat and to drink with them.

en.L: And his sons would go and hold a feast in the house of each one on his day, and they would send and invite their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.
en.B: His sons used to take turns holding a feast, each in his own house on his day, and they would send for their three sisters and invite them to eat and drink with them.
en.R: Job's sons took turns holding feasts in their homes, each on his own day. They would invite their three sisters to come and eat and drink with them.

es.L: Y sus hijos iban y hacían un banquete en la casa de cada uno en su día, y enviaban a llamar a sus tres hermanas para que comieran y bebieran con ellos.
es.B: Sus hijos solían turnarse para dar un banquete, cada uno en su casa en el día que le tocaba, y mandaban a buscar a sus tres hermanas y las invitaban a comer y beber con ellos.
es.R: Los hijos de Job se turnaban para hacer fiestas en sus casas, cada uno en su día. Invitaban a sus tres hermanas a comer y beber con ellos.

fr.L: Et ses fils allaient faire un festin dans la maison de chacun, à son jour ; et ils envoyaient inviter leurs trois sœurs à manger et à boire avec eux.
fr.B: Ses fils avaient coutume de donner tour à tour un festin, chacun dans sa maison, au jour qui était le sien, et ils faisaient venir leurs trois sœurs pour manger et boire avec eux.
fr.R: Les fils de Job organisaient chacun leur tour une fête chez eux, chacun son jour. Ils invitaient leurs trois sœurs à venir manger et boire avec eux.

sw.L: Na wanawe walikuwa wakienda na kufanya karamu katika nyumba ya kila mmoja siku yake; nao walituma na kuwaalika dada zao watatu kula na kunywa pamoja nao.
sw.B: Wanawe walikuwa na desturi ya kufanya karamu kwa zamu, kila mmoja nyumbani kwake siku yake, nao waliwatumia dada zao watatu ujumbe na kuwaalika kula na kunywa pamoja nao.
sw.R: Wana wa Ayubu walifanya karamu kwa zamu nyumbani kwao, kila mmoja siku yake. Waliwaalika dada zao watatu waje kula na kunywa pamoja nao.

vi.L: Và các con trai ông thường đi và mở tiệc tại nhà của mỗi người vào ngày của mình; và họ sai người mời ba chị em gái của họ đến ăn và uống với họ.
vi.B: Các con trai ông thường lần lượt mở tiệc, mỗi người tại nhà mình vào ngày của mình, và họ sai người đi mời ba chị em gái đến cùng ăn uống với họ.

ko.L: 그의 아들들이 가서 각자 자기 날에 자기 집에서 잔치를 베풀고, 사람을 보내어 그들의 세 누이를 불러 함께 먹고 마시게 하곤 했다.

pt.L: E os seus filhos iam e faziam um banquete na casa de cada um, no seu dia; e mandavam chamar as suas três irmãs para comerem e beberem com eles.
pt.B: Os seus filhos costumavam dar banquetes, um de cada vez, cada um na sua casa e no seu dia, e mandavam chamar as três irmãs para comer e beber com eles.
pt.R: Os filhos de Jó se revezavam para dar festas, cada um na sua casa e no seu dia. Eles convidavam as três irmãs para vir comer e beber com eles.

decisions.choice: would go and hold: a regular custom, not one event
decisions.reason: The verbs have the form Hebrew narrative uses for what happened again and again (as also in 1:5). The verse describes the family's way of life before the disasters: the brothers met in turn and included their sisters.

decisions.choice: on his day: each son's turn, perhaps his birthday
decisions.reason: "His day" most likely means the day each son's turn came round. In 3:1 "his day" is Job's birthday, so some take it here as each son's birthday, which would make the feasts spread through the year. The text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: a feast: a banquet with drinking
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to drink" and names a festive meal with wine (1:13; Esther 1:3; Judges 14:10). The feasting itself is not condemned; it is the setting for Job's care in the next verse.

decisions.choice: used to take turns; took turns (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "take turns" to make clear what "each on his day" means; Literal keeps the Hebrew's "would go and hold a feast".

records.literal_gloss: And it was when had gone round [the] days of the feast, and sent Job and sanctified them, and rose early in the morning and offered up burnt offerings [according to the] number of all of them; for said Job, perhaps have sinned my sons and blessed God in their heart. Thus did Job all the days.

en.L: And it was, when the days of feasting had gone their round, that Job would send and consecrate them; and he would rise early in the morning and offer burnt offerings according to the number of them all. For Job said, "Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts." This is what Job did all the days.
en.B: Whenever a round of feasting was over, Job would send for his children and consecrate them. He would get up early in the morning and offer a burnt offering for each one of them, because Job said to himself, "Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts." This is what Job always did.
en.R: When each round of feasts was over, Job would send for his children and make them ready to worship God. Early in the morning he would offer a burnt offering for each of them. Job thought, "Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts." Job always did this.

es.L: Y sucedía que, cuando los días del banquete habían cumplido su vuelta, Job enviaba por ellos y los santificaba; y se levantaba de madrugada y ofrecía holocaustos conforme al número de todos ellos. Porque Job decía: «Quizá mis hijos han pecado y han maldecido a Dios en su corazón». Así hacía Job todos los días.
es.B: Cada vez que terminaba una ronda de banquetes, Job mandaba llamar a sus hijos y los consagraba. Se levantaba temprano por la mañana y ofrecía un holocausto por cada uno de ellos, porque Job se decía: «Tal vez mis hijos han pecado y han maldecido a Dios en su corazón». Esto es lo que Job hacía siempre.
es.R: Cuando terminaba cada ronda de fiestas, Job mandaba llamar a sus hijos y los preparaba para adorar a Dios. Muy de mañana ofrecía un holocausto por cada uno de ellos. Job pensaba: «A lo mejor mis hijos han pecado y han maldecido a Dios en su corazón». Job siempre hacía esto.

fr.L: Et il arrivait, quand les jours de festin avaient achevé leur tour, que Job les envoyait chercher et les consacrait ; puis il se levait de bon matin et offrait des holocaustes d’après leur nombre à tous. Car Job disait : « Peut-être mes enfants ont-ils péché et maudit Dieu dans leur cœur. » Ainsi faisait Job tous les jours.
fr.B: Chaque fois qu’un tour de festins était terminé, Job faisait venir ses enfants et les consacrait. Il se levait tôt le matin et offrait un holocauste pour chacun d’eux, car Job se disait : « Peut-être mes enfants ont-ils péché et maudit Dieu dans leur cœur. » Voilà ce que Job faisait toujours.
fr.R: Quand une série de fêtes était terminée, Job faisait venir ses enfants et les préparait à adorer Dieu. Tôt le matin, il offrait un holocauste pour chacun d’eux. Job pensait : « Mes enfants ont peut-être péché et maudit Dieu dans leur cœur. » Job faisait toujours cela.

vi.L: Và khi các ngày tiệc tùng đã xoay vòng xong, Gióp sai gọi họ đến và biệt họ ra thánh; rồi ông dậy sớm vào buổi sáng và dâng các của lễ thiêu theo số của tất cả họ. Vì Gióp nói: "Biết đâu các con tôi đã phạm tội và đã nguyền rủa Đức Chúa Trời trong lòng." Gióp làm như vậy mọi ngày.

vi.R: Mỗi lần các buổi tiệc xong một vòng, Gióp cho gọi các con đến và chuẩn bị cho họ sẵn sàng thờ phượng Đức Chúa Trời. Sáng sớm, ông dâng một của lễ thiêu cho mỗi người con. Gióp nghĩ: "Biết đâu các con mình đã phạm tội và nguyền rủa Đức Chúa Trời trong lòng." Gióp luôn làm như vậy.

ko.L: 잔치 날들이 한 차례 돌고 나면, 욥은 사람을 보내어 그들을 거룩하게 하였고, 아침 일찍 일어나 그들 모두의 수대로 번제를 드렸다. 욥이 "혹시 내 자식들이 죄를 짓고 마음속으로 하나님을 저주하였을지도 모른다." 하고 말했기 때문이다. 욥은 모든 날 동안 이렇게 행하였다.
ko.B: 잔치가 한 차례 끝날 때마다 욥은 자식들을 불러 거룩하게 하였다. 그는 아침 일찍 일어나 자식들 하나하나를 위해 번제를 드렸다. 욥은 속으로 "혹시 내 자식들이 죄를 짓고 마음속으로 하나님을 저주했을지도 모른다." 하고 생각했기 때문이다. 욥은 언제나 이렇게 했다.
ko.R: 잔치가 한 바퀴 돌고 나면, 욥은 자식들을 불러서 하나님께 예배드릴 준비를 하게 했다. 그리고 아침 일찍 자식들 한 명 한 명을 위해 번제를 드렸다. 욥은 "내 자식들이 죄를 짓고 마음속으로 하나님을 저주했을지도 몰라." 하고 생각했다. 욥은 늘 이렇게 했다.

pt.L: E acontecia que, quando os dias do banquete tinham completado a sua volta, Jó mandava [chamá-los] e os consagrava; e se levantava cedo de manhã e oferecia holocaustos segundo o número de todos eles. Porque Jó dizia: "Talvez os meus filhos tenham pecado e amaldiçoado a Deus no seu coração." Assim fazia Jó todos os dias.
pt.B: Sempre que terminava uma rodada de banquetes, Jó mandava chamar os filhos e os consagrava. Levantava-se cedo de manhã e oferecia um holocausto por cada um deles, pois Jó dizia consigo mesmo: "Talvez os meus filhos tenham pecado e amaldiçoado a Deus no coração." Era isso que Jó fazia sempre.
pt.R: Quando terminava cada rodada de festas, Jó mandava chamar os filhos e os preparava para adorar a Deus. De manhã bem cedo, ele oferecia um holocausto por cada um deles. Jó pensava: "Talvez os meus filhos tenham pecado e amaldiçoado a Deus no coração." Jó sempre fazia isso.

decisions.choice: cursed God: the verb is "bless", used in place of "curse"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb here is the ordinary word for "bless", but the sense is its opposite: Job fears his children have cursed God, a sin that would call for sacrifice. Writers and scribes avoided putting the words "curse God" into the text, and wrote "bless" instead; the same substitution is made in 1 Kings 21:10, 13, where Naboth is falsely accused of having "blessed" God and the king, a crime punished by death. Job uses it in this sense in 1:11, 2:5 and 2:9 as well. Since the same verb can also be said when taking leave of someone (Genesis 47:10), a few have read it as "said goodbye to God", but "curse" fits every use in the prologue. Where the verb is a real blessing (1:10, 21; 42:12) the context makes it plain.

decisions.choice: consecrate them and offer burnt offerings: Job acts as priest of his household
decisions.reason: To consecrate people is to make them ritually ready to come before God, usually by washing and setting themselves apart (Exodus 19:10, 14; 1 Samuel 16:5). The head of the family then offered the sacrifices himself, as Noah and Abraham did (Genesis 8:20; 22:13), with no priest or sanctuary mentioned. A burnt offering was wholly burned on the altar (Leviticus 1).

decisions.choice: my children: sons and daughters
decisions.reason: The plural of "son" often means children of both sexes (Genesis 30:1). The daughters ate and drank at the feasts too (1:4), and Job offers sacrifices "according to the number of them all", so he most likely has all ten in mind.

decisions.choice: Job did this all the days: his regular practice
decisions.reason: The verb form describes repeated action, and "all the days" means always. Job's care reaches even to sins of the heart that no one could see; the narrator shows this before the test begins.

decisions.choice: Job said (Literal); said to himself (Balanced); thought (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb "say" often means to say to oneself, to think (Genesis 20:11). Balanced and Readable make clear that Job was not speaking to anyone.

decisions.choice: the satan: a title, "the adversary" or "the accuser", one who opposes in a court
decisions.reason: The noun has the article, "the satan", and Hebrew does not put the article on personal names, so here it is a title or role rather than a name. The word means one who stands against someone: the LORD's angel stands in Balaam's way "as an adversary" (Numbers 22:22, 32), and in a court the satan is the accuser who stands at a man's right hand (Psalm 109:6; Zechariah 3:1-2). In Job he is one of the heavenly beings who come before the LORD, he questions Job's motives, and he can act only as far as the LORD allows (1:12; 2:6). Later Scripture uses the word as a name, Satan, for God's great enemy (1 Chronicles 21:1, without the article; Revelation 12:9), and many readers identify him with this figure. The book of Job itself does not develop that; it presents him as the accuser in the heavenly court.

decisions.choice: the sons of God: heavenly beings, members of God's council
decisions.reason: In Hebrew "son of" often means "belonging to the class of". The sons of God here are heavenly beings who serve God and gather before him as courtiers before a king, like the host of heaven standing by the LORD's throne in 1 Kings 22:19-22. Job 38:7 has them shouting for joy when the earth was founded, and Psalm 29:1 and 89:7 use a similar phrase for the heavenly beings. They are not human beings.

decisions.choice: present themselves before the LORD: come to stand before the king of heaven
decisions.reason: The verb is used of officials and servants taking their places before a ruler to report and receive orders (Zechariah 6:5, of riders who present themselves "before the Lord of all the earth"; Proverbs 22:29). The scene has moved from Job's house to the court of heaven, which Job never learns about.

decisions.choice: and it was the day: one day
decisions.reason: This is the usual Hebrew way to begin a new scene on a particular day (1:13; 2:1; 1 Samuel 1:4; 2 Kings 4:8). It does not mean a fixed festival.

decisions.choice: the satan (Literal); the Accuser (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the satan", with the article and lowercase, to show it is a title. Balanced and Readable translate the title as "the Accuser", capitalized because it is used as his name in this story; "Satan" would make it a personal name, which the article rules out here.

decisions.choice: the heavenly beings (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Sons of God" can suggest a family of gods or human believers to a new reader. Readable says who they are; Literal and Balanced keep "the sons of God".

decisions.reason: As in the published Vietnamese books: the reader setting shows "CHÚA" or the name "Gia-vê". "Đức Chúa Trời", "Đấng Toàn Năng" and "Chúa" render El, Eloah, Shaddai and Adonai and take no span.

decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the article, so this is a title, not a name (meaning decision m1). Literal writes "kẻ sa-tan" in lowercase as a title; Balanced and Readable translate it, as Revelation 12:10 says "kẻ tố cáo". "Sa-tan", the name used in 1 Chronicles 21:1, would make it a personal name.

decisions.reason: As in the published Korean books: the reader setting shows "주" or the name "야훼". "하나님", "전능자" and "주님" render El, Eloah, Shaddai and Adonai and take no span.

decisions.choice: "그 사탄" (L); "고발자" (B, R); "하나님의 아들들" (L, B), "하늘의 존재들" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the article, so this is a title, not a name (meaning decision m1); Literal shows the article with "그", and Balanced and Readable translate the title, as Revelation 12:10 speaks of the one who accuses.

decisions.choice: "o Satanás" (L); "o acusador" (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (1:6-2:7). The Hebrew has the article, so it is a title, not a name (m1). Literal keeps the article, "o Satanás", so the reader sees the word later tradition made a name while the article shows it is still a role; 1 Chronicles 21:1, where there is no article, writes plain "Satanás". Balanced and Readable translate the title as "o acusador", lowercase because Portuguese writes a role that way ("o acusador dos nossos irmãos", Revelation 12:10), where the English capitalizes "the Accuser".

decisions.choice: "os filhos de Deus" (L, B), "os seres celestiais" (R); YHWH as {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}
decisions.reason: For the whole book: "os filhos de Deus" at Literal and Balanced (also 2:1 and 38:7), with no gender span, since Portuguese "filhos" here names a class of beings (m2); Readable says who they are, as the English Readable does. The divine name takes the setting span only where the Hebrew has YHWH (the prose frame, 12:9, 38:1, 40:1-6, 42); El, Eloah and Elohim are "Deus" and Shaddai "o Todo-Poderoso", with no span.

source.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־הַשָּׂטָ֖ן מֵאַ֣יִן תָּבֹ֑א וַיַּ֨עַן הַשָּׂטָ֤ן אֶת־יְהוָה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר מִשּׁ֣וּט בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּמֵֽהִתְהַלֵּ֖ךְ בָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said YHWH to the satan, from where do you come? And answered the satan YHWH and said, from roaming on the earth and from walking about on it.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to the satan, "From where do you come?" And the satan answered {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, "From roaming on the earth, and from walking about on it."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to the Accuser, "Where have you come from?" The Accuser answered {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "From roaming the earth and walking up and down on it."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} asked the Accuser, "Where have you been?" The Accuser answered, "I have been going all over the earth, walking back and forth across it."

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo al satán: «¿De dónde vienes?». Y el satán respondió {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y dijo: «De rondar por la tierra y de andar de un lado a otro por ella».
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo al Acusador: «¿De dónde has venido?». El Acusador respondió {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «De recorrer la tierra y andar de aquí para allá por ella».
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le preguntó al Acusador: «¿Dónde has estado?». El Acusador respondió: «He estado recorriendo toda la tierra, yendo de un lado a otro».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit au satan : « D’où viens-tu ? » Et le satan répondit {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} et dit : « De rôder sur la terre et d’y circuler. »
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à l’Accusateur : « D’où viens-tu ? » L’Accusateur répondit {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « De rôder sur la terre et d’y aller et venir. »
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a demandé à l’Accusateur : « Où étais-tu ? » L’Accusateur a répondu : « J’ai parcouru toute la terre, j’y suis allé de long en large. »

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia yule satani, "Unatoka wapi?" Naye yule satani akamjibu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akasema, "Kutoka kuranda-randa duniani, na kutembea-tembea juu yake."
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Mshtaki, "Umetoka wapi?" Mshtaki akamjibu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Nimekuwa nikizurura duniani na kutembea juu na chini ndani yake."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwuliza Mshtaki, "Ulikuwa wapi?" Mshtaki akajibu, "Nimekuwa nikizunguka dunia yote, nikitembea huku na kule."

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với kẻ sa-tan: "Ngươi từ đâu đến?" Và kẻ sa-tan thưa với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} rằng: "Từ việc lang thang trên đất và đi lại trên đó."
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán hỏi Kẻ Tố Cáo: "Ngươi từ đâu đến?" Kẻ Tố Cáo thưa với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Tôi vừa rong ruổi khắp đất và đi tới đi lui trên đó."
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hỏi Kẻ Tố Cáo: "Ngươi đã ở đâu?" Kẻ Tố Cáo thưa: "Tôi đã đi khắp mặt đất, đi tới đi lui khắp nơi."

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그 사탄에게 말씀하셨다. "너는 어디에서 오느냐?" 그러자 그 사탄이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 대답하여 말했다. "땅 위를 두루 다니다가, 그 위를 거닐다가 왔습니다."
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 고발자에게 물으셨다. "어디에서 왔느냐?" 고발자가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 대답했다. "땅을 두루 돌아다니며 이리저리 거닐다가 왔습니다."
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 고발자에게 물으셨다. "어디에 있다 왔느냐?" 고발자가 대답했다. "온 땅을 돌아다녔습니다. 이곳저곳을 오가며 다녔습니다."

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse ao Satanás: "De onde vens?" E o Satanás respondeu {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} e disse: "De percorrer a terra e de andar por ela."
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} perguntou ao acusador: "De onde vens?" O acusador respondeu {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}: "De percorrer a terra, andando por ela de um lado para o outro."
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} perguntou ao acusador: "Por onde andaste?" O acusador respondeu: "Estive andando pela terra toda, indo e vindo por ela."

decisions.choice: roaming and walking about: going to and fro over the earth, as one on patrol
decisions.reason: The first verb means to go back and forth, rove; it is used of the LORD's eyes that range over all the earth (2 Chronicles 16:9; Zechariah 4:10). The second is used of the riders in Zechariah 1:10-11 whom the LORD sends "to walk about through the earth" and who report back. The satan speaks like an inspector who has been watching the earth and is ready to report.

decisions.choice: From where do you come?: the opening of a report, not a request for information
decisions.reason: The LORD's question opens the conversation, as a king asks a servant for his report; the narrator does not suggest the LORD did not know. The same exchange is repeated in 2:2.

decisions.choice: the Accuser answered (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable leaves out the repeated name of the LORD after "answered" and turns the reply into a full sentence ("I have been ..."), which is clearer for new readers.

decisions.choice: God says "ngươi" to the Accuser; the Accuser says "tôi" and speaks to God as "Ngài", "Chúa"
decisions.reason: The heavenly court is pictured as a king's audience: the LORD speaks as master, the Accuser as a subordinate reporting to him, without the warmth of "con", which Job uses before God.

decisions.choice: God speaks to the Accuser in 해라체 with "너"; the Accuser answers in 합쇼체 with "주님" and "저"
decisions.reason: A king's audience: the LORD speaks as master, the Accuser reports as a subordinate, as servants speak to God elsewhere in the Korean Old Testament.

decisions.choice: God says "tu" to the satan; the satan says "tu" to God (1:10-12; 2:2-6)
decisions.reason: Following docs/portuguese-style.md section 4: God speaks to one person with "tu", and anyone who speaks to God uses "tu", whatever his attitude. The words around it show the challenge in the satan's speech; the form of address does not change.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־הַשָּׂטָ֔ן הֲשַׂ֥מְתָּ לִבְּךָ֖ עַל־עַבְדִּ֣י אִיּ֑וֹב כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין כָּמֹ֨הוּ֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ אִ֣ישׁ תָּ֧ם וְיָשָׁ֛ר יְרֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְסָ֥ר מֵרָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: And said YHWH to the satan, have you set your heart on my servant Job? For there is none like him on the earth, a man blameless and upright, fearing God and turning aside from evil.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to the satan, "Have you set your heart on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave Job? For there is none like him on the earth, a man blameless and upright, who fears God and turns away from evil."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to the Accuser, "Have you considered {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Job? There is no one like him on earth: a man blameless and upright, who fears God and turns away from evil."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to the Accuser, "Have you noticed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Job? There is no one on earth like him. He is blameless and upright. He honors God and keeps away from evil."

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo al satán: «¿Has puesto tu corazón en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} esclavo Job? Porque no hay nadie como él en la tierra, hombre íntegro y recto, que teme a Dios y se aparta del mal».
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo al Acusador: «¿Te has fijado en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo Job? No hay nadie como él en la tierra: es un hombre íntegro y recto, que teme a Dios y se aparta del mal».
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo al Acusador: «¿Has notado a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo Job? No hay nadie en la tierra como él. Es íntegro y recto. Honra a Dios y se aleja del mal».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit au satan : « As-tu posé ton cœur sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} esclave Job ? Car il n’y a personne comme lui sur la terre, un homme intègre et droit, qui craint Dieu et se détourne du mal. »
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à l’Accusateur : « As-tu prêté attention à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur Job ? Il n’a pas son pareil sur terre : c’est un homme intègre et droit, qui craint Dieu et se détourne du mal. »
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit à l’Accusateur : « As-tu vu {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur Job ? Personne sur la terre ne lui ressemble. Il est intègre et droit. Il honore Dieu et se tient loin du mal. »

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia yule satani, "Je, umeweka moyo wako juu ya mtumwa {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Ayubu? Kwa maana hakuna aliye kama yeye duniani, mtu mkamilifu na mnyofu, anayemcha Mungu na kujiepusha na uovu."
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Mshtaki, "Je, umemfikiria mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Ayubu? Hakuna mtu kama yeye duniani: ni mtu mkamilifu na mnyofu, anayemcha Mungu na kujiepusha na uovu."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Mshtaki, "Je, umemwona mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Ayubu? Hakuna mtu duniani aliye kama yeye. Yeye ni mkamilifu na mnyofu. Anamheshimu Mungu na kukaa mbali na uovu."

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với kẻ sa-tan: "Ngươi có để lòng đến nô lệ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Gióp không? Vì trên đất không có ai như người, một người trọn vẹn và ngay thẳng, kính sợ Đức Chúa Trời và lánh xa điều ác."
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Kẻ Tố Cáo: "Ngươi có lưu tâm đến đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Gióp chăng? Trên đất chẳng có ai bằng người: một người trọn vẹn và ngay thẳng, kính sợ Đức Chúa Trời và lánh xa điều ác."
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Kẻ Tố Cáo: "Ngươi có thấy đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Gióp không? Trên đất không ai giống như người. Người trọn vẹn và ngay thẳng. Người tôn kính Đức Chúa Trời và tránh xa điều ác."

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그 사탄에게 말씀하셨다. "너는 내 종 욥에게 네 마음을 두었느냐? 땅 위에 그와 같은 자가 없으니, 흠 없고 정직하며, 하나님을 경외하고 악에서 떠난 사람이다."
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 고발자에게 말씀하셨다. "너는 내 종 욥을 눈여겨보았느냐? 땅 위에 그만한 사람이 없다. 그는 흠 없고 정직하며, 하나님을 경외하고 악에서 떠난 사람이다."
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 고발자에게 말씀하셨다. "너는 내 종 욥을 보았느냐? 세상에 그런 사람은 없다. 그는 흠 없고 정직하다. 그는 하나님을 두려운 마음으로 섬기고 악한 일을 멀리한다."

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse ao Satanás: "Puseste o teu coração sobre o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} escravo Jó? Porque não há ninguém como ele na terra, homem íntegro e reto, que teme a Deus e se desvia do mal."
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} disse ao acusador: "Prestaste atenção no {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Jó? Não há ninguém como ele na terra: um homem íntegro e reto, que teme a Deus e se desvia do mal."
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} disse ao acusador: "Reparaste no {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Jó? Não há ninguém na terra como ele. Ele é íntegro e reto. Honra a Deus e se mantém longe do mal."

decisions.choice: set your heart on: give your attention to, consider
decisions.reason: "To set the heart on" means to pay attention to something (1 Samuel 9:20; Job 34:14). Here it may also hint at watching someone closely, the satan's role as one who looks for faults; the LORD himself raises Job's name.

decisions.choice: my servant Job: one who belongs to the LORD and serves him; a title of honor
decisions.reason: The word is used of a slave or servant who belongs to a master. Spoken by the LORD of a person, it is a title of honor, given to Abraham, Moses and David (Genesis 26:24; Numbers 12:7; 2 Samuel 7:5). The LORD calls Job "my servant" again at the end of the book (42:7-8).

decisions.choice: blameless and upright ...: the LORD repeats the narrator's words of 1:1
decisions.reason: The description is word for word that of 1:1. What the narrator said, the LORD now confirms. See 1:1 for the sense of "blameless and upright".

decisions.choice: slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As throughout the project, Literal keeps "slave" for this word so its hard edge is visible, while Balanced and Readable say "servant", which is how a title of honor is heard in English.

decisions.choice: set your heart on (Literal); considered (Balanced); noticed (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom instead of its picture.

decisions.choice: "종" at every level
decisions.reason: Korean "종" covers both the slave who belongs to a master and the honoured servant of God, so one word serves all three levels where the English has "slave" (L) and "servant" (B, R).

records.literal_gloss: And answered the satan YHWH and said, [is it] for nothing [that] fears Job God?

en.L: And the satan answered {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, "Is it for nothing that Job fears God?"
en.B: The Accuser answered {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Does Job fear God for nothing?"
en.R: The Accuser answered {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Does Job honor God without getting anything for it?"

es.B: El Acusador respondió {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «¿Es que Job teme a Dios sin sacar nada?».
es.R: El Acusador respondió {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «¿Acaso Job honra a Dios sin recibir nada a cambio?».

fr.B: L’Accusateur répondit {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « Job craint-il Dieu pour rien ? »
fr.R: L’Accusateur a répondu {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « Est-ce que Job honore Dieu sans rien recevoir en échange ? »

sw.B: Mshtaki akamjibu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Je, Ayubu anamcha Mungu bila faida yoyote?"
sw.R: Mshtaki akamjibu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Je, Ayubu anamheshimu Mungu bila kupata chochote?"

vi.B: Kẻ Tố Cáo thưa với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Gióp kính sợ Đức Chúa Trời mà chẳng được gì sao?"
vi.R: Kẻ Tố Cáo thưa với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Gióp tôn kính Đức Chúa Trời mà không nhận được gì sao?"

ko.L: 그러자 그 사탄이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 대답하여 말했다. "욥이 하나님을 경외하는 것이 거저입니까?"
ko.B: 고발자가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 대답했다. "욥이 아무 대가도 없이 하나님을 경외하겠습니까?"
ko.R: 고발자가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 대답했다. "욥이 아무것도 받지 않고 하나님을 두려운 마음으로 섬기겠습니까?"

pt.L: E o Satanás respondeu {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} e disse: "É de graça que Jó teme a Deus?"
pt.B: O acusador respondeu {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}: "Será que Jó teme a Deus por nada?"
pt.R: O acusador respondeu {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}: "Será que Jó honra a Deus sem ganhar nada com isso?"

decisions.choice: for nothing: without payment, with nothing to gain
decisions.reason: The word means "freely, for no pay" (Genesis 29:15, of working for nothing) and also "without cause". The satan asks whether Job's devotion is free or bought by his blessings: take the rewards away, he suggests, and the devotion will go too. This is the question the whole book tests. In 2:3 the LORD turns the same word back on him: Job was ruined "for nothing", without cause.

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no
decisions.reason: The question is not a request for information but a challenge: Job does not, the satan implies, fear God for nothing. The next two verses give his reasons.

decisions.choice: honor God without getting anything for it (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "honor" as in 1:1 and spells out what "for nothing" means here.

decisions.choice: "de graça" (L); "por nada" (B); "sem ganhar nada com isso" (R)
decisions.reason: The word means "freely, without pay" (m1). "De graça" is exactly that in Portuguese, and "por nada" says it in Balanced as a question about motives; "em vão" would mean "to no purpose", which is not the satan's point, and "debalde" is archaic.

source.text: הֲלֹֽא־אַ֠תָּה שַׂ֣כְתָּ בַעֲד֧וֹ וּבְעַד־בֵּית֛וֹ וּבְעַ֥ד כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֖וֹ מִסָּבִ֑יב מַעֲשֵׂ֤ה יָדָיו֙ בֵּרַ֔כְתָּ וּמִקְנֵ֖הוּ פָּרַ֥ץ בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is it] not you [who] have put a hedge around him and around his house and around all that [is] his, round about? The work of his hands you have blessed, and his livestock has spread out in the land.

en.L: Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not put a hedge around him and around his house and around all that he has, on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his livestock has spread out in the land.
en.B: Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not put a protective hedge around him and his household and everything he owns on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his flocks and herds have spread throughout the land.
en.R: You have put a wall of protection around him, his family and everything he owns. You have blessed everything he does, and his animals have spread all over the land.

es.L: ¿No has puesto {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} un cerco alrededor de él, de su casa y de todo lo que tiene, por todos lados? Has bendecido la obra de sus manos, y su ganado se ha extendido por la tierra.
es.B: ¿No has levantado {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} un cerco protector a su alrededor, alrededor de su familia y de todo lo que posee? Has bendecido el trabajo de sus manos, y sus rebaños y manadas se han esparcido por todo el país.
es.R: Tú lo has rodeado de un muro de protección a él, a su familia y a todo lo que tiene. Has bendecido todo lo que hace, y sus animales se han extendido por toda la tierra.

fr.L: N’as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pas mis une haie autour de lui, autour de sa maison et autour de tout ce qui est à lui, tout alentour ? Tu as béni l’œuvre de ses mains, et son troupeau s’est répandu dans le pays.
fr.B: N’as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pas dressé une haie protectrice autour de lui, de sa famille et de tous ses biens, de tous côtés ? Tu as béni le travail de ses mains, et ses troupeaux se sont multipliés dans tout le pays.
fr.R: Tu l’as entouré d’un mur de protection, lui, sa famille et tout ce qu’il possède. Tu as béni tout ce qu’il fait, et ses bêtes se sont répandues dans tout le pays.

sw.L: Je, si {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} uliyemwekea uzio pande zote, yeye na nyumba yake na vyote alivyo navyo? Umeibariki kazi ya mikono yake, na mifugo yake imeenea katika nchi.
sw.B: Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} hukumwekea uzio wa ulinzi kila upande, yeye na jamaa yake na vyote anavyomiliki? Umebariki kazi ya mikono yake, na makundi yake ya kondoo na ng'ombe yameenea kote nchini.
sw.R: Umemzungushia ukuta wa ulinzi yeye, familia yake na kila kitu alicho nacho. Umebariki kila anachofanya, na wanyama wake wameenea kila mahali katika nchi.

vi.L: Chẳng phải chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã rào chung quanh người, chung quanh nhà người và chung quanh mọi điều người có, khắp bốn bề sao? Ngài đã ban phước cho công việc tay người làm, và gia súc người đã lan tràn trong xứ.
vi.B: Chẳng phải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã rào giữ người, gia đình người và mọi thứ người có ở khắp mọi phía sao? Ngài đã ban phước cho công việc tay người làm, và bầy chiên bầy bò của người sinh sôi khắp xứ.
vi.R: Ngài đã dựng một bức tường che chở người, gia đình người và mọi thứ người có. Ngài ban phước cho mọi việc người làm, và súc vật của người lan ra khắp xứ.

ko.L: 주님께서 그와 그의 집과 그에게 속한 모든 것을 사방으로 울타리로 두르지 않으셨습니까? 주님께서 그의 손이 하는 일에 복을 주셨고, 그의 가축은 땅에 퍼졌습니다.
ko.B: 주님께서 그와 그의 집안과 그가 가진 모든 것을 사방으로 울타리를 쳐서 지켜 주지 않으셨습니까? 주님께서 그가 손대는 일마다 복을 주셔서, 그의 양 떼와 소 떼가 온 땅에 퍼졌습니다.
ko.R: 주님께서 그와 그의 가족과 그의 모든 재산을 담으로 둘러 지켜 주셨습니다. 그가 하는 모든 일에 복을 주셨고, 그의 짐승들은 온 땅에 늘어났습니다.

pt.L: Não puseste {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} uma cerca ao redor dele, e ao redor da sua casa, e ao redor de tudo o que ele tem, de todos os lados? Abençoaste a obra das mãos dele, e o seu gado se espalhou pela terra.
pt.B: Não foste {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} que o cercaste de proteção, a ele, à sua família e a tudo o que ele tem, por todos os lados? Abençoaste o trabalho das mãos dele, e os seus rebanhos e manadas se espalharam por toda a terra.
pt.R: Tu puseste um muro de proteção ao redor dele, da família dele e de tudo o que ele tem. Abençoaste tudo o que ele faz, e os animais dele se espalharam por toda a terra.

decisions.choice: put a hedge around him: protected him on every side
decisions.reason: A hedge of thorns kept animals and thieves out of a field or vineyard (Isaiah 5:5; Proverbs 15:19). The satan means that God has shielded Job, his family and his property from all harm. Job later uses a related verb for the opposite feeling, that God has "hedged him in" (3:23).

decisions.choice: you have blessed the work of his hands: a real blessing, prosperity in all he does
decisions.reason: Here the verb "bless" has its plain sense, as in Deuteronomy 28:12 ("to bless all the work of your hand"). The satan admits Job's prosperity comes from God, and that is his complaint: the blessing explains the devotion.

decisions.choice: Have you not ...?: a question expecting the answer yes
decisions.reason: The Hebrew stresses "you": it is God himself who has protected Job. The question is a way of stating the fact.

decisions.choice: statement instead of question (Readable)
decisions.reason: The question expects "yes", so Readable states it directly, which is easier to follow.

decisions.choice: his flocks and herds have spread (Balanced); his animals (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word for livestock covers flocks and herds together (1:3); "spread out" means grown in number and spread over the land (Genesis 30:30, 43).

source.text: וְאוּלָם֙ שְֽׁלַֽח־נָ֣א יָֽדְךָ֔ וְגַ֖ע בְּכָל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֑וֹ אִם־לֹ֥א עַל־פָּנֶ֖יךָ יְבָרֲכֶֽךָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: But stretch out, please, your hand and touch all that [is] his; if not to your face he will bless you.

en.L: But stretch out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand, please, and touch all that he has, [and see] if he will not curse {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face!
en.B: But stretch out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand and strike everything he has, and he will surely curse {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face.
en.R: But reach out and take away everything he has. Then he will curse {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face!

es.L: Pero extiende ahora {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} mano y toca todo lo que tiene, [y verás] si no {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} maldice en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} cara.
es.B: Pero extiende {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} mano y golpea todo lo que tiene, y de seguro {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} maldecirá en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} cara.
es.R: Pero extiende la mano y quítale todo lo que tiene. ¡Entonces {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} maldecirá en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} cara!

fr.L: Mais étends donc {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main et touche à tout ce qui est à lui, [et tu verras] s’il ne {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} maudit pas à {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} face !
fr.B: Mais étends {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main et frappe tout ce qu’il possède : il {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} maudira sûrement en face.
fr.R: Mais avance la main et prends-lui tout ce qu’il a. Alors il {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} maudira en face !

sw.L: Lakini nyoosha basi mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, uguse vyote alivyo navyo, [uone] kama hatakulaani mbele ya uso {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}!
sw.B: Lakini nyoosha mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} upige vyote alivyo navyo, naye hakika atakulaani ana kwa ana.
sw.R: Lakini nyoosha mkono uchukue kila kitu alicho nacho. Hapo ndipo atakulaani waziwazi!

vi.L: Nhưng xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hãy giơ tay ra và đụng đến mọi điều người có, [xem] người có nguyền rủa {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngay trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không!
vi.B: Nhưng xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hãy giơ tay ra đánh vào mọi thứ người có, chắc chắn người sẽ nguyền rủa {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngay trước mặt.
vi.R: Nhưng xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hãy ra tay lấy đi mọi thứ người có. Rồi người sẽ nguyền rủa {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngay trước mặt!

ko.L: 그러나 부디 주님의 손을 펴서 그에게 속한 모든 것을 건드려 보십시오. 그가 주님 앞에서 대놓고 주님을 저주하지 않나 [보십시오]!
ko.B: 그러나 주님께서 손을 펴서 그가 가진 모든 것을 치시면, 그는 틀림없이 주님 앞에서 대놓고 주님을 저주할 것입니다.
ko.R: 그러나 주님께서 손을 뻗어 그가 가진 모든 것을 빼앗아 보십시오. 그러면 그는 주님 앞에서 대놓고 주님을 저주할 것입니다!

pt.L: Mas estende, por favor, a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} mão e toca em tudo o que ele tem, [e verás] se ele não {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} amaldiçoa na {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} cara!
pt.B: Mas estende a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} mão e fere tudo o que ele tem, e com certeza ele {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} amaldiçoará na {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} cara.
pt.R: Mas estende a mão e tira dele tudo o que ele tem. Então ele vai {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} amaldiçoar na {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} cara!

decisions.choice: he will curse you: the verb is "bless", meaning "curse"
decisions.reason: As in 1:5, the verb for "bless" stands in place of "curse" (see the note there). The satan's claim is that Job will turn on God openly.

decisions.choice: if he will not ...: an oath, meaning "he will surely ..."
decisions.reason: "If not" is the form of an oath whose curse is left unsaid ("may it be so to me, if he does not ..."); it makes a strong statement, "he certainly will" (Numbers 14:28). The same words return in 2:5.

decisions.choice: touch: strike, harm; to your face: openly
decisions.reason: "Touch" with God's hand means to strike with harm (Genesis 26:11; Job 19:21, "the hand of God has touched me"). "To your face" means openly, defiantly, not in secret as Job feared his children might in their hearts (1:5).

decisions.choice: reach out and take away (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "stretch out your hand and touch" means here: the satan asks God to take Job's possessions from him.

decisions.choice: na tua cara
decisions.reason: "To your face" means openly and defiantly (m3). "Na tua cara" is how Portuguese says that, with the same insolence; "na tua face" is only the picture.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־הַשָּׂטָ֗ן הִנֵּ֤ה כָל־אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ֙ בְּיָדֶ֔ךָ רַ֣ק אֵלָ֔יו אַל־תִּשְׁלַ֖ח יָדֶ֑ךָ וַיֵּצֵא֙ הַשָּׂטָ֔ן מֵעִ֖ם פְּנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said YHWH to the satan, see, all that [is] his [is] in your hand; only against him do not stretch out your hand. And went out the satan from with [the] face of YHWH.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to the satan, "Look, all that he has is in your hand; only against him do not stretch out your hand." And the satan went out from the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to the Accuser, "Very well, everything he has is in your power. Only do not lay a hand on the man himself." Then the Accuser went out from the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to the Accuser, "All right. You may do what you want with everything he has. But you must not harm Job himself." So the Accuser left the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo al satán: «Mira, todo lo que tiene está en tu mano; solo contra él no extiendas tu mano». Y el satán salió de delante de la presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo al Acusador: «Está bien, todo lo que tiene está en tu poder. Solo que no pongas la mano sobre él mismo». Entonces el Acusador salió de la presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo al Acusador: «De acuerdo. Puedes hacer lo que quieras con todo lo que tiene. Pero no le hagas daño a Job mismo». Así que el Acusador se retiró de la presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit au satan : « Voici, tout ce qui est à lui est dans ta main ; seulement, contre lui n’étends pas ta main. » Et le satan sortit de devant la face {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à l’Accusateur : « Soit ! Tout ce qu’il possède est en ton pouvoir. Seulement, ne porte pas la main sur lui-même. » Et l’Accusateur se retira de la présence {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit à l’Accusateur : « D’accord. Tu peux faire ce que tu veux de tout ce qu’il a. Mais tu ne dois pas toucher à Job lui-même. » Alors l’Accusateur a quitté la présence {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia yule satani, "Tazama, vyote alivyo navyo vimo mkononi mwako; ila juu yake yeye usinyooshe mkono wako." Naye yule satani akatoka mbele ya uso wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Mshtaki, "Haya, vyote alivyo navyo viko katika uwezo wako. Ila usimguse yeye mwenyewe." Kisha Mshtaki akaondoka mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Mshtaki, "Sawa. Unaweza kufanya lolote unalotaka na vyote alivyo navyo. Lakini usimdhuru Ayubu mwenyewe." Basi Mshtaki akaondoka mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với kẻ sa-tan: "Kìa, mọi điều người có đều ở trong tay ngươi; chỉ có điều, chống lại người thì ngươi chớ giơ tay ra." Và kẻ sa-tan đi ra khỏi trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Kẻ Tố Cáo: "Được, mọi thứ người có đều ở trong quyền ngươi. Chỉ đừng tra tay trên chính bản thân người." Rồi Kẻ Tố Cáo lui ra khỏi trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Kẻ Tố Cáo: "Được thôi. Ngươi muốn làm gì với mọi thứ người có cũng được. Nhưng ngươi không được làm hại chính Gióp." Vậy Kẻ Tố Cáo rời khỏi trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그 사탄에게 말씀하셨다. "보아라, 그에게 속한 모든 것이 네 손에 있다. 다만 그를 향해서는 네 손을 뻗지 마라." 그러자 그 사탄이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 얼굴 앞에서 나갔다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 고발자에게 말씀하셨다. "좋다. 그가 가진 모든 것을 네 권한에 맡긴다. 다만 그 사람 자신에게는 손을 대지 마라." 그러자 고발자가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 물러갔다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 고발자에게 말씀하셨다. "좋다. 그가 가진 모든 것은 네가 원하는 대로 해도 된다. 그러나 욥 자신은 해치지 마라." 그래서 고발자는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 떠나갔다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse ao Satanás: "Eis que tudo o que ele tem [está] na tua mão; somente contra ele não estendas a tua mão." E o Satanás saiu da presença {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} disse ao acusador: "Pois bem, tudo o que ele tem está em teu poder. Somente não estendas a mão contra ele mesmo." Então o acusador saiu da presença {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} disse ao acusador: "Está bem. Podes fazer o que quiseres com tudo o que ele tem. Mas não faças mal ao próprio Jó." Então o acusador se retirou da presença {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.

decisions.choice: in your hand: in your power
decisions.reason: To be "in someone's hand" is to be under his control, to do with as he likes (Genesis 16:6; Genesis 39:4).

decisions.choice: only not against him: the satan acts only within the limit the LORD sets
decisions.reason: The satan can do nothing to Job without the LORD's permission, and the LORD sets the boundary: Job's possessions, not his body. In 2:6 the limit is moved but still kept: his body, not his life. The text does not explain why the LORD allows the test; the book leaves that question open for Job and the reader to wrestle with.

decisions.choice: went out from the presence of the LORD: left the audience
decisions.reason: "From with the face of" means from being in someone's presence, as one leaves a king's court (Genesis 4:16; 41:46). The heavenly scene closes, and the satan goes out to act.

decisions.choice: Look (Literal); Very well ... in your power (Balanced); All right. You may do what you want (Readable)
decisions.reason: The particle "see" here grants the request; Balanced and Readable render it as consent and give the sense of "in your hand".

source.text: וַיְהִ֖י הַיּ֑וֹם וּבָנָ֨יו וּבְנֹתָ֤יו אֹֽכְלִים֙ וְשֹׁתִ֣ים יַ֔יִן בְּבֵ֖ית אֲחִיהֶ֥ם הַבְּכֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was the day, and his sons and his daughters [were] eating and drinking wine in [the] house of their brother the firstborn.

en.L: And the day came when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their brother, the firstborn.
en.B: One day Job's sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their oldest brother.

decisions.choice: Sheba: the Sabeans, a people of Arabia, here as raiders
decisions.reason: Sheba was a people of Arabia known for trade caravans (6:19; 1 Kings 10:1-2; Ezekiel 27:22). The name stands for the people, with a singular verb, "Sheba fell on them". Here they come as raiders from the desert.

decisions.choice: the young men: Job's servants
decisions.reason: The word means young men, and is often used of servants, as here the herdsmen and plowmen. In 1:19 the same word refers to Job's sons and daughters.

decisions.choice: with the edge of the sword: literally "to the mouth of the sword"
decisions.reason: The sword is pictured as a mouth that devours (Genesis 34:26; Joshua 6:21). The phrase means they were killed without mercy.

decisions.choice: I alone have escaped to tell you: the refrain of the four reports
decisions.reason: Each messenger ends with the same words (1:15, 16, 17, 19), and each arrives while the last is still speaking. The repetition gives the effect of blow after blow with no time to take in one loss before the next. The servant who survives exists only to carry the news.

decisions.choice: the Chaldeans: tribes of the land along the lower Euphrates, here as raiders
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans are the people of southern Mesopotamia (Genesis 11:28, "Ur of the Chaldeans"), who later ruled Babylon. Here they appear as raiding bands from the desert to the east, not as an empire. The four disasters alternate: raiders (1:15), fire from the sky (1:16), raiders (1:17), wind (1:19).

decisions.choice: formed three companies: split into three groups
decisions.reason: "Heads" here means divisions of an armed band (Judges 7:16; 9:43; 1 Samuel 11:11). Attacking from three sides was a way to surround and take a large herd.

decisions.choice: I alone have escaped to tell you: the refrain of the four reports
decisions.reason: Each messenger ends with the same words (1:15, 16, 17, 19), and each arrives while the last is still speaking. The repetition gives the effect of blow after blow with no time to take in one loss before the next. The servant who survives exists only to carry the news.

decisions.choice: the young people: Job's sons and daughters
decisions.reason: The word is the same as "young men" in 1:15-17, but here it refers to those eating in the house, Job's children (1:18). Its masculine plural form covers the daughters too.

decisions.choice: a great wind from across the wilderness striking the four corners: a desert storm
decisions.reason: Violent winds came in from the desert east of the settled land (Jeremiah 4:11; 13:24; Hosea 13:15). A wind that strikes all four corners at once is a whirlwind, which brought the whole house down.

decisions.choice: struck: the same verb as "touch" in 1:11

decisions.choice: tore his robe and shaved his head: signs of mourning
decisions.reason: Tearing one's clothes and shaving the head were ways of showing grief at a death or disaster (Genesis 37:34; Jeremiah 41:5; Micah 1:16). The robe was the outer garment worn by a man of rank.

decisions.choice: fell to the ground and worshiped: bowed face down before God
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow low, often lying face down, before a king or before God; it is the usual word for worship. The satan expected Job to curse God (1:11); instead he worships.

decisions.choice: to show his grief; worshiped God (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says why Job tore his robe and shaved his head, which a new reader may not know, and names God as the one he worshiped, which the verse implies.

decisions.choice: "se prostrou" (L); "adorou" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the bodily act of bowing down that is also the word for worship (m2). Literal says the act, "se prostrou", after "caiu por terra"; Balanced and Readable say "adorou", as the English does.

decisions.choice: naked I will return there: I will leave the world with nothing, as I came
alternatives: return to the womb of the earth
decisions.reason: Job pictures his birth and his death as two journeys with nothing in his hands (Ecclesiastes 5:14, numbered 5:15 in many Bibles, uses the same picture). "There" cannot mean his mother's womb; it is most likely the earth, from which human beings were taken and to which they return (Genesis 3:19), pictured as a mother's womb (Psalm 139:15). The point is that everything he lost was given, not owned.

decisions.choice: the LORD gave and the LORD has taken: Job sees the LORD's hand behind his losses
decisions.reason: Job does not blame raiders, fire or wind but traces both his blessings and his losses to the LORD, and the narrator approves (1:22). He does not know of the satan's part, and the book never tells him. Here Job uses the divine name, which in the speeches of the book is rare (12:9).

decisions.choice: may the name of the LORD be blessed: real blessing, praise
decisions.reason: The verb is the one the satan said Job would use as a curse (1:11). Job uses it in its true sense: he praises the LORD. The "name" stands for the LORD himself as he is known.

decisions.choice: set in four lines
decisions.reason: The saying has the balance of Hebrew poetry: two lines on birth and death, two on the LORD's giving and taking. The lines follow the verse's Hebrew accents (the main division after "has taken", lesser ones after "my mother's womb" and "there"). The rest of chapters 1-2 is prose.

decisions.choice: I had nothing when I was born ... when I die; praised (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of nakedness and of returning "there". It says "praised" for the verb here so that it is not confused with "blessed" in the sense of being given good things.

decisions.choice: Job's words in the plain style, with no hearer addressed
decisions.reason: Job is not speaking to anyone present; the plain style suits a cry spoken aloud, and the last line is a wish, not a prayer addressed to the LORD.

decisions.choice: "Nu saí ... e nu voltarei para lá", "tomou", "bendito seja" (L); "Saí nu ... e nu vou voltar", "tirou", "que o nome ... seja bendito" (B); "louvado" (R)
decisions.reason: Drafted from the Hebrew, not from a familiar version. Literal keeps the Hebrew's order, with "nu" first in both lines and the wish verb before "the name"; Balanced puts the words in ordinary Portuguese order and turns the wish into "que ... seja bendito". "Para lá" keeps the Hebrew's "there", which means the earth (m1), as the English does. The verb "bless" here is real praise (m3), so Readable says "louvado", as the English Readable says "praised". Set in four lines, as each English level.

records.literal_gloss: In all this not sinned Job, and not he ascribed wrongdoing to God.

en.L: In all this Job did not sin, and he did not ascribe anything unseemly to God.
en.B: In all this Job did not sin or accuse God of wrongdoing.
en.R: Even after all this, Job did not sin. He did not blame God for doing anything wrong.

es.L: En todo esto Job no pecó, y no le imputó a Dios nada impropio.
es.B: En todo esto Job no pecó ni acusó a Dios de haber obrado mal.
es.R: Aun después de todo esto, Job no pecó. No culpó a Dios de hacer nada malo.

fr.L: Dans tout cela, Job ne pécha pas, et il n’imputa à Dieu rien d’inconvenant.
fr.B: Dans tout cela, Job ne pécha pas et n’accusa pas Dieu d’avoir mal agi.
fr.R: Même après tout cela, Job n’a pas péché. Il n’a pas reproché à Dieu d’avoir fait quelque chose de mal.

vi.B: Trong mọi điều ấy, Gióp không phạm tội và không cáo buộc Đức Chúa Trời làm điều sai trái.

pt.L: Em tudo isso Jó não pecou, nem atribuiu a Deus coisa alguma imprópria.
pt.B: Em tudo isso Jó não pecou nem acusou Deus de injustiça.
pt.R: Mesmo depois de tudo isso, Jó não pecou. Ele não disse que Deus tinha feito algo errado.

decisions.choice: did not ascribe anything unseemly to God: did not accuse God of wrong
alternatives: did not charge God with folly
decisions.reason: The rare noun means something unseemly or offensive, what is morally tasteless (24:12; Jeremiah 23:13). "To give" it to God means to say that God acted improperly. Job grieves, but he does not accuse God.

decisions.choice: in all this Job did not sin: the narrator's verdict on the first test
decisions.reason: The narrator answers the satan's prediction (1:11): Job did not curse God. A similar verdict closes the second test (2:10).

decisions.choice: anything unseemly (Literal); wrongdoing (Balanced); anything wrong (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the sense of what is improper; Balanced and Readable say what the phrase amounts to.
